faqLeft.q: What engine does the Land Rover Freelander 2.0 Di / Td4 use?
faqLeft.a: It depends on the year. Early cars (roughly 1997 to 2001) use the L-Series diesel. Later cars (roughly 2001 to 2006) use the BMW M47D20 — the same engine found in BMW 3 and 5 Series of that era. Send us your registration and we'll confirm which one your car has.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Land Rover Freelander 2.0 Di / Td4 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £1,900, for either engine code. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.

faqLeft.q: Which engine code is fitted to my Freelander?
faqLeft.a: Enter your registration on this page and we'll confirm whether you have the L-Series or the BMW M47D20 before you're quoted anything.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild L-Series Freelander 2.0 Di engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The L-Series was fitted to early Freelander 2.0 Di models, and we rebuild them to the same standard as the later M47D20 units.

faqLeft.q: Do you rebuild BMW M47D20 Freelander 2.0 Td4 engines?
faqLeft.a: Yes. We replace timing chain components, bearings and gaskets as standard on every M47D20 rebuild.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Freelander 2.0 Di / Td4 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Freelander if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does a Freelander 2.0 Di / Td4 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most Freelander owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history, and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty — often longer and more comprehensive than what a used engine supplier offers.
